title: Janus connector: incremental embed sink with monotonic checkpoints
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Our current embed ingestion pathways are fragmented: streaming HTTP/GRPC acceptors commit to a store in different ways (some write small files to S3, others push to Kafka), clients need idempotency guidance, and we lack a single bridge that provides ordered, checkpointable ingestion suitable for both low-latency streaming and high-throughput bulk jobs. This results in duplicate vectors, out-of-order commits, and complex consumer logic in the vectorizer and reranker pipelines.

Goal: Build the 'Janus connector' — a sink adapter that accepts streaming and batched embed upload requests, emits monotonic opaque checkpoint tokens to clients, and writes a deterministic commit log that downstream workers can convert to batch jobs with strong deduplication and ordering semantics. The connector must work for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (avoid managed-only primitives).

Design summary:
- API: single ingestion endpoint (HTTP/GRPC) that accepts single items, small batches (<=512), and streaming chunked requests. Each successful write returns a monotonic checkpoint token: "epoch:shard:seq" (opaque string clients may persist). Clients can resume from a token for incremental resends.
- Deterministic chunking: Each incoming item is assigned a stable chunk key computed from (client_id || content_hash || epoch_window). This ensures identical payloads map to same chunk within a retention window for dedup.
- Idempotency: Support client-provided idempotency-key and server-assigned monotonic checkpoint. Server dedup uses (shard, chunk_key, idempotency_key) windows. Deduplication TTL configurable per tenant.
- Commit log semantics: Append-only, per-shard, monotonic sequence numbers. Implementation uses write-ahead objects in S3 with compacted manifests for Private deployments; in Hosted we optionally use Kafka/managed stream. The log contains minimal metadata (seq, timestamp, chunk_key, payload_ref) to keep small objects and cheap listing.
- Exactly-once ingest for downstream: Downstream vectorizer workers will perform idempotent commits to vector DB using the (chunk_key, payload_ref) deterministic key. A final 'commit manifest' operation atomically marks a log range as processed to prevent double-processing on retries.
- Backpressure and acceptance latency: API should accept small writes in <100ms (ack), and provide best-effort admission control (quota tokens, per-tenant buffers). Large bulk uploads are staged as async jobs (job_id returned) and materialized into the commit log in streaming-friendly chunks.
- Failure & retries: Clients can re-send from the last checkpoint. Server-side retries are idempotent. For prolonged outages the job semantics degrade to at-least-once with a reconciliation pass that uses chunk_key and content-hash to dedup.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end test that a client can stream 50k small items, crash, resume from a returned checkpoint and see no duplicates in final vector DB (run on staging).
2) API accepts single-item writes with median ack <60ms and 95th <150ms for normal-tenant loads.
3) Bulk job path ingests 1M vectors/hour per 8-shard connector in scale test.
4) Integration with reranking eval harness: ensure reranker tests show no quality regression after dedup/ordering changes.
5) Expose metrics: committed_seq, lag_by_shard, dup_count, avg_ack_latency, last_checkpoint_per_tenant.

Migration notes: We will build a migration shim to convert existing S3/Kafka artifacts into Janus commit manifests; this will be a separate ticket.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement tenant-level encryption key rotation for archived commit logs (follow-up).
